13. My issue wise findings are as under : Issue No.1 Whether the petitioner is entitled to maintenance from the respondent as prayed for ?
If so at what rate and for what term ?
OPP Undisputedly defendant/respondent is natural father of plaintiff Ms. Radhika Kumari.

Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 reads as under : "20. Maintenance of children and aged parents.
(1) Subject to the provisions of this section a Hindu is bound, during his or her lifetime, to maintain his or her legitimate or illegitimate children and his or her aged or infirm parents.

(2) A legitimate or illegitimate child may claim maintenance from his or her father or Kumari Radhika (Minor) Aged About 7 ... vs Shri Arun Kumar Sharma on 15 April, 2011 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140377794/

(3) The obligation of a person to maintain his or her aged or infirm parent or a daughter who is unmarried extends in so far as the parent or the unmarried daughter, as the case may be, is unable Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain himself or herself out of his or her own earnings or other property.
Explanation.
In this section "parent" includes a childless stepmother."
Further liability of mother and father to maintain the children is joint and several.

In this case, Ms. Radhika Kumari is residing with her Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East,

Vibha Sharma is without any substance in as much as at no point of time defendant availed lawful remedies for securing the custody of Ms. Radhika Kumari and his petition u/s. 9 of Hindu Marriage Act was, admittedly, withdrawn by him.

Radhika Kumari.(A. Annamalai Mudaliar Vs. Perumaves Ammal and others.

In Kirtikumer D. Vadodaria v. State of Gujarat (1996) 4 SCC 479 it was held in paragraph 8 of the Report :
"According to the Law of the Land with regard to maintenance, there is an obligation of the husband Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi to maintain his wife which does not arise by reason of any contract - express or implied - but out of jural relationship of husband and wife consequent to the performance of marriage.

sentences.text: Such as obligation of the husband to maintain his wife arises irrespective of the fact whether he has no property, as it is considered an imperative duty and a solemn obligation of the husband to maintain his wife.
The husband cannot be heard saying that he is unable to maintain due to financial constraints so long as he is capable of earning.

Further, according to Section 20 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, a Hindu is under a legal obligation to maintain his wife, minor sons,
unmarried daughters and aged or infirm parents.

The obligation to maintain them is personal, legal and absolute in character and arises from the very existence of the relationship between the parties."
13.

Section 23 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act 1956 reads as under : "23. Amount of maintenance.

(1) It shall be in the discretion of the Court to determine whether any, and if so what,
maintenance shall be awarded under the provisions of this Act, and in doing so, the court shall have due regard to the considerations set out in subsection (2), or sub section (3), as the case may be,
so far as they are applicable.

sentences.text: However, there is no provisions in the Act as to who out of mother and father is more liable.
Since the liability rests on both, it means, it is coextensive and none can avoid his or her liability by taking the excuse that maintenance should be claimed from the other.
This matter rests on the discretion of the Court which will, of course, be exercised judiciously.
Also section 20, unlike section 18 relating to the right of wife for maintenance, does not mention the grounds on which the claim for maintenance can be made.
It casts an absolute obligation on the part of the parents.
Hence burden is on the parent to establish in an action to maintenance that there is no default on his or her part.

Even in the cases covered by the latter part of subsection (3) of section 20, the parent should prove that the major daughter who is unmarried has her own earnings or other property to maintain herself.

It admits no ambiguity that the obligation of the parents is personal, absolute and Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East,
Delhi does not depend upon the possession of property.
In the case in hand Ms. Vibha Sharma is Double M.A. B. Ed.
She is practicing as an advocate.

As per affidavit Ex. P1, plaintiff has no source of income except Rs.500/ per month granted by the Court in case u/s. 125 Cr. PC which is not sufficient to maintain the plaintiff and plaintiff is fully dependent upon the poor grand maternal parents.
Also as per plaintiff, defendant is not paying the abovesaid Rs.500/ per month regularly.
More specifically respondent has not paid the said Rs.500/ per month since August 2007.
Plaintiff is claiming maintenance @ Rs.5,000/ Per Month.
The depositions made in Ex. P1 have gone uncontroverted/unrebutted.
It is pertinent to note that affidavit Ex. P1 is silent about the income of Ms. Vibha Sharma, natural mother of plaintiff.

Obviously Ms. Vibha Sharma is able to earn handsome amount of money due to her qualifications &
her being an advocate by profession.
Further as per defendant Ms. Vibha Sharma is having rental income after the death of her parents/father.
Ms. Vibha Sharma is under no less a legal obligation to maintain her minor daughter Ms. Radhika Kumari than the defendant.

Liability to maintain Ms.
Radhika Kumari is coextensive on Ms. Vibha Sharma and the defendant/respondent.
Smt. Vibha Sharma, however, has Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi concealed her own income.
Be that as it may.
Further stand of plaintiff/Smt. Vibha Sharma is that defendant is a man of means who is running his clinic.

Also, as alleged, defendant is owning 50 Bighas of agricultural land at his native village vide Ex. PW1/B and Ex. PW1/C & is having income of Rs.1 lac per annum from the said land Respondent, as alleged, is earning Rs.40,000/ per month.
The above averments/depositions have been denied by defendant.

To prove the above stand plaintiff has relied upon the affidavit of Ms.

No other corroborative evidence has been brought on judicial file.

Property at Delhi is Anand Swaroop Aggarwal SCJCumRC:East, Delhi also alleged to have been disposed of by defendant.
